transcript.text: Mara, before Ruth gives her fire safety report, I'd like to respond to Dev's question about the load-spreading deck and the stunt lane. The 30-millimeter load-spreading deck I tested was designed to distribute the modular painted-timber set's dead load across Soundstage 3's floor to keep us under the 600 kilograms-per-square-meter limit. My load test confirmed that the deck performs adequately for that purpose. However, I want to be straightforward with the group: my test focused on the set's static load. Dev is asking about a live load — a horse's weight plus a rider dismounting onto a 2-meter crash mat concentrated at the landing end of the lane. That's a dynamic load scenario I have not yet specifically tested. I'd recommend we either run a targeted supplemental load test for that stunt lane area before fabrication begins, or I can model the dynamic load and provide written confirmation. I don't want to give a blanket safety sign-off on the horse dismount without that additional analysis. The deck surface itself should be able to receive a non-slip treatment or overlay, but I'd want to verify that any added material doesn't compromise the load-spreading performance. So my recommendation is: the modular painted-timber option with the 30-millimeter deck is structurally viable for the set itself, but the stunt lane area needs a dedicated supplemental structural review before I can sign off on the horse dismount.
